co_icebox_the.blurb: A compact granite cliff on the far bank of the South Platte in Elevenmile Canyon, facing the Pine Cone Dome side. Seventeen routes, mostly bolted sport with a handful of trad lines, and the grade spread leans hard: a few moderate climbs in the 5.6 to 5.9 range, then a solid block of 5.11s and 5.12s, topped by a couple of 5.13s. The wall steepens as you go up and turns overhanging toward its right end, so expect sustained, pumpy climbing rather than a beginner crag. Climbers report the 5.10s staying shaded in summer, and an ice flow high on the right can linger into spring, hence the name.

co_loch_vale_gorge.blurb: A winter ice and mixed venue in Rocky Mountain National Park, reached from the Glacier Gorge or Bear Lake side, with cliffs wrapping the east and north flanks of Thatchtop at roughly 10,000 feet. Terrain runs from low-angle slabs and thin mixed lines to free-hanging pillars and pure ice falls, plus a top-rope zone. Of seventeen climbs, most are ice from WI3 to WI5, with a few mixed routes from M4 to M7 and one rock line. Shaded and cold, it holds ice well but is among the busiest spots in the park when conditions are good, so plan on sharing the base with other parties.

co_tan_buttresses_the.blurb: High-alpine granite buttresses forming the north rim of the Black Wall cirque above Chicago Lakes, below Gray Wolf Peak in the Mount Blue Sky area. Seventeen mostly multi-pitch trad routes sit at around 12,700 feet, with grades concentrated in the 5.9 and 5.10 range, a handful of 5.11s and a single 5.12. Expect clean, crack-and-face granite and committing alpine days instead of short cragging. Plan for thin air, route-finding and protection that needs attention, and fast-building afternoon storms. It is a full hike in, and a poor choice for beginners.
co_tan_buttresses_the.approach: Hike the climbers' trail from Summit Lake up the Spaulding line toward the Black Wall, cross the top of that wall, then drop down a ramp and ledge system to the base. Drop big packs once you top out on the ramp.

co_cabin_wall.blurb: A long sandstone cliff in Escalante Canyon, west of Grand Junction, sitting above a historic cabin beside the canyon road. It is a crack climber's wall: sixteen trad routes and a single aid line, running from about 5.7 up to 5.12, with the bulk in the 5.9 to 5.11 range. Many lines have no bolted anchors, so bring a full rack and be ready to build your own. The sandstone is soft and easily damaged when wet, so let it dry for a day or two after rain.

co_liberty_cap.blurb: A sandstone buttress in the Redlands side of Colorado National Monument near Grand Junction, tucked up Ute Canyon. Mostly trad, with a bit of sport, one top-rope and a lone boulder problem, it offers single-pitch crack lines in the 5.10 and 5.11 range plus one 5.12. Desert tower-and-crack character, comparable to Utah. Fall through spring is the comfortable window, since summer runs hot. The sandstone is soft and weakens badly when wet, so wait until it has dried before leaving the ground. Reaching it means a moderate hike that steepens near the end.
